title: Tileable image generation is the Achilles' Heel of genAI in gamedev
author: mankrip
selftext:
I have yet to find an image generator where I can upload my own image, ask it to make the image tileable, and get correct results where I can use the resulting image as a seamless repeating texture in a 3D surface.

This shows that the companies developing genAI tools have ZERO knowledge of the actual needs of game developers. Sure, I can get some nifty results, but getting those results to be actually useful in a game still requires a massive amount of tedious work that the AI should have taken care of.

It's even worse for videos, because not only all the genAI tools I tried can't generate tileable videos, they also can't make the videos loop seamlessly from the last frame to the first.

Does anyone know a tool that actually works, or is the situation really this bad?

replies.author: mankrip
replies.body:
It's only trivial to do without ai if the source image is trivial.

It's absolutely not trivial for images with highly specific details like this, and specially when the lighting isn't perfectly uniform across edges.

https://preview.redd.it/zqiahkw3l9yg1.jpeg?width=6271&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=ae16ee6efe2ca62967e4f7e609dbe98ea8e799ff

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
If you have photoshop, the details and lighting don't matter. Load image into photoshop, use offset filter at half the dimensions, use generative fill on the seams, reverse the offset. It's a bit weird to have tiling people, but it's quite doable. If you don't have Photoshop or if generative fill is struggling in understanding the image or if you don't have access to Photoshop and need to use something like Krita, then run the offset, export the image and inpaint the seams instead with your favorite image program (or get something like nano banana to just fix the seamed part. You can then choose to reverse the offset at that point or keep it as it is. The edges should properly tile because when you did the offset you basically shift the contents so that the edges are seamless.

I'd say it's still rather trivial as far as art and graphic design is concerned.  Yeah it's more than just hitting a 'generate' button. But... it could be a lot worse.

comments.author: JjyKs
comments.body:
Making tileable textures with AI doesn't differ a single bit from making tileable texture from a photo which is probably the most common way the photorealistic textures are made. For simple wall/ground textures it can be automated completely without AI after the imagegen itself and the results look really good. I've built this exact feature straight into my engine where I can just describe a texture I want, it adds a master prompt for graphical style and then generates the texture. After that it runs through some code that makes it tileable and allows me to tweak the positioning and scale if needed.  
  
For anything harder like the picture of people you posted, a tileable texture is IMO completely wrong approach unless you're intentionally developing for some old console that lacks proper sprite functionality. You can ask AI to generate a cutoff mask and just programmatically cut the people off the image based on that. Even fill in the legs etc that are missing in the original image, so you can place them with more freedom if wanted. Then just generate some filler background like concrete if needed and place the people on top of that on the game engine side.
